Item: SGCC Legacy Synthetic F1=1.00 vs Real F1=0.36-0.41
Reason_for_Discrepancy: Initial phase used 1,500-sample synthetic dataset generated by generate_sample_data.py with deterministic zero-injection for theft. Real dataset contains genuine human consumption noise and 95%+ class distribution overlap.
Resolution: Real SGCC dataset was acquired and validated on Sept 16, 2026. All synthetic results are archived as historical artifacts. Real baseline is authoritative.

Reason_for_Discrepancy: Result A was evaluated during preliminary development on an unstratified split or validation holdout with trapezoidal PR-AUC integration. Result B represents the strict double-sealed test partition (N=6,356, seed 42) evaluated strictly once without threshold retuning at default t=0.50 using Average Precision.
Resolution: Result B (F1=0.3592, PR-AUC=0.3114) is the authoritative double-sealed test benchmark. Result A is classified as a preliminary development benchmark.

Item: SGCC Chronological vs Lexicographical Column Ordering
Reason_for_Discrepancy: Raw CSV header stored date strings alphabetically. Extracting diff() or applying forward-fill without sorting would compute transitions across non-adjacent calendar dates.
Resolution: Programmatic chronological date parsing and sorting was implemented in run_fe_real_pipeline.py, resolving all temporal order errors.

Item: UCI XGBoost Time-Series CV MAE (10,365.77 kWh) vs Validation MAE (3,935.63 kWh)
Result_A: CV Mean MAE = 10,365.77 kWh, Std = 10,204.25 kWh
Reason_for_Discrepancy: During 2011, many of the 370 customer meters were offline or unmetered (2011 mean load was 122,713 kWh). In early 2012, meters came online, doubling load to 212,317 kWh. In expanding TimeSeriesSplit, Fold 2 trained on 2011 (max load ~193,000 kWh) and tested on 2012 (max load 448,000 kWh). Tree-based models cannot extrapolate above training maximums, generating Fold-2 MAE of 37,169.66 kWh! In post-2012 stationary splits (Validation and Test), XGBoost achieves 3,935 - 4,503 kWh.
Resolution: The discrepancy is mathematically proven to be a structural non-stationarity artifact of 2011 customer meter onboarding in TimeSeriesSplit. Post-2012 validation and test metrics are authoritative.

Item: UCI Sealed Test Window Boundary (4,503.51 kWh vs 4,421.55 kWh)
Reason_for_Discrepancy: Result A was evaluated over the full chronological test partition from July 1, 2014 00:00 to Dec 31, 2014 23:00 (4,416 hours). Result B trimmed the initial 24 hours of the test split to avoid lag warm-up boundary effects (4,392 hours).
Resolution: Both numbers reflect valid windows; Result A is the official full-test benchmark (N=4,416), while Result B is the boundary-trimmed secondary benchmark (N=4,392).
